name: AOI01 Chibabel: Chókwè, Macia and Xai-Xai, Mozambique

reference.product: Delineation (DEL), monitoring 0, version 1, scored only where it agrees with the First Estimate Product (FEP) from Sentinel-1 at 16:22 UTC on 16 Jan (observed 20,126.9 ha)

method.name: lightgbm
method.summary: LightGBM classifier on 14 radar features (HH, HV, HV minus HH, the change between dates, and 5x5 local mean and spread), each scene's land median removed; flood where the probability is at least 0.37; not water on 5 Jan (DSWx-S1, or JRC occurrence >= 4% where DSWx-S1 has no data); not permanent water (JRC occurrence >= 50%).

aoi05_test.decision_rule: higher AOI05 IoU at 3 decimals wins; a tie keeps the rule

legend.2: #bdbdbd at alpha 170: valid, outside the area both Copernicus maps cover, or where the 16 and 18 Jan maps disagree
legend.3: #e6ab02 at alpha 170: unclear: HH rose, possible flooded vegetation
legend.4: #7570b3 at alpha 170: edge buffer, not scored

limits: NISAR Beta data: not fully calibrated. The 17 Jan scene is about 3 dB brighter overall, so each scene's median over reference land is removed before the classifier sees it.

Agreement with Copernicus, not accuracy, and a lower bound: no Copernicus map was made on the NISAR morning here. The reference maps are from about 11 hours before (Sentinel-1, C-band) and 35 hours after (COSMO-SkyMed, X-band) the NISAR pass, so part of their difference may be the sensor, not the flood.
NISAR's last pass on this track was 17 Jan 03:42 UTC. Copernicus observed a larger flood here on 20 Jan (127,755.1 ha), after that pass.
Pixels where HH rose by more than 3 dB (possible flooded vegetation) are not scored. This method only finds open water.
Permanent water (JRC occurrence >= 50%) is never counted as flood.
A 2-pixel band along the Copernicus mapped-area edge is not scored. Flood polygon edges are scored.
The classifier learned from the Copernicus map of AOI06 only.

Only pixels where both maps agree are scored. They disagree on 37% of the area both cover (mostly flooded on 18 Jan only), and those pixels count as outside the mapped area. The red overlay shows flood on both maps (17,569 ha on this grid), not the full 18 Jan extent.
DSWx-S1 covers only 32% of this area on 5 Jan. Elsewhere, water before the flood is JRC occurrence >= 4%, the level that best matches DSWx-S1 where both exist (IoU 0.38).
On the held-out area AOI05, the tuned rule scored IoU 0.521 and LightGBM 0.572 against Copernicus, so the LightGBM classifier is used.
Against this area's reference, the tuned rule scores IoU 0.833 and LightGBM 0.718. The method was chosen on AOI05, not here.
9,050 ha (18%) of the detected new water was already dark in NISAR's 5 Jan image. DSWx-S1 (or JRC) called it dry, so it counts as new, but some of it may have been water before 17 Jan.

Buildings: 313 OpenStreetMap buildings sit inside detected new water, out of 346,003 mapped on this grid. This is a lower bound: OpenStreetMap is incomplete here, a 30 m pixel is larger than a house, and flooded built-up areas look bright in radar, so open-water detection misses them. It says nothing about damage. Data: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
